title: Module quiz: Model choice, cost and migration

questions.stem: A support product sends one payload to several targets, and the same payload suddenly fails on the newest with a 400 about `temperature`. Which design stops the failure at its root?

options.text: Catch the 400 and resend the body with the field removed after each failure
options.says: Ruled out because a rejected setting fails every time and a 400 is "the signal of a rejected parameter", not something to patch after each failure.

options.text: Build each request per model, omitting what that model rejects
options.says: The page says to "Change the request builder together with the id" and that Haiku 4.5 "still accepts sampling parameters", so one body does not fit every model.

options.text: Fix the parameter at one custom value for every model in the catalog
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is "Omit temperature, top_p, and top_k, or leave them at their defaults: any other value is rejected", so one custom value fails on the newest model.

options.text: Pin the older target for good, so that the payload keeps working there
options.says: Ruled out because a pinned older model still reaches retirement, after which "Requests to retired models will fail", so pinning for good only postpones the break

questions.stem: A nightly bulk job and a chat feature both use a mid-size model. Finance asks which figure to track per feature. What does the module support?

options.text: Tokens counted before sending, summed at the end of each month
options.says: Ruled out because "The token count is an estimate" of input only, and output and cache split appear only in usage.

options.text: Price per million tokens from the list, taken from the pricing page
options.says: Ruled out because the tokenizer difference makes "the price per token a poor proxy for the price per task".

options.text: Cost per request, priced from usage with the multipliers applied
options.says: The page gives the cost per request as a sum over the usage fields and says "These multipliers stack with other pricing modifiers such as the Batch API discount and data residency."

options.text: Output tokens only, since they carry the highest unit price
options.says: Ruled out because a usage has "four input-side fields at three prices", so output alone is incomplete.

questions.stem: A router moves a long conversation to a different target halfway through, and answer quality drops. Which cause does the module name?

options.text: The retirement notice reset the cache of the conversation
options.says: Ruled out because the page never ties a retirement notice to a cache, and says only that notice is "at least 60 days' notice".

options.text: The new model has a different alias that resolves to an old snapshot
options.says: Ruled out because "Every Claude model ID is a pinned snapshot" and a dateless id is its own snapshot.

options.text: The token counting endpoint rejected the longer conversation
options.says: Ruled out because the endpoint rejects inputs such as "server tools like web search", not long conversations.

options.text: The new model reads the earlier turns without the earlier reasoning
options.says: The page quotes "A router or fallback that moves a conversation from Claude Opus 5.5 to any other model runs those turns without them."

origin.section: Routing: the cheapest model that can do each request

questions.stem: A plan to move 20 percent of traffic to a replacement model on Monday and the rest at the end of the week is proposed. What should the team add before Monday?

options.text: A second evaluation on the vendor's published benchmark suite
options.says: Ruled out because the page's step is an evaluation "on your own cases", not a published suite.

options.text: An evaluation on its own cases, run ahead of the shift
options.says: The page says to evaluate "on your own cases" and warns that migrating on the retirement date "leaves no time to evaluate".

options.text: A new tokenizer, so the counts match across both models
options.says: Ruled out because "A new tokenizer changes token counts" and belongs to the model, so the team re-checks budgets and does not install one.

options.text: A larger `max_tokens` on every request, to leave room for thinking
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Re-measure instead of copying numbers" and gives no blanket increase.
